bullets.title: META: Cloud Compute Launch Sparks AI Infrastructure Debate; JPM Downgrades to Neutral
bullets.body: META announced plans to build 'Meta Compute,' a cloud infrastructure business to sell excess AI compute capacity and models to third parties, driving a +9% stock rally while triggering a -13-17% selloff in neoclouds CRWV and NBIS (META >50% and 33% of their backlogs, respectively). JPMorgan downgraded META to Neutral ($725 PT) preferring META develop AI products for its 4B users rather than sell infrastructure; MS (OW, $775 PT) models every 250 MW leased at $40/W adds ~$3 (8%) to 2028 EPS; Citi (Buy, $850 PT) sees Meta Compute as FCF accelerant. Mizuho/KeyBanc/Jefferies all maintain Buy/OW ratings arguing capex trajectory is unchanged and cloud optionality improves ROIC narrative.

bullets.title: MSFT: Wolfe Cuts PT to $525 on Capex/Memory Cost Shock; Job Cuts Announced
bullets.body: Wolfe Research cuts MSFT PT to $525 from $570 (Outperform) as memory price increases force FY27 capex to $270B (vs. $230B prior), FY27 FCF flips to -$17.4B from prior +$14.7B, and gross margin drops to 63.1% vs. consensus 66.6%. Separately, MSFT announced job cuts affecting <2.5% of its 220K workforce across sales, consulting, and Xbox. MSFT trades at 19x CY27 P/E, a 20% discount to Mega Cap peers.

bullets.title: NVDA: Revenue-Sharing Model Launched; Remains Top Mega-Cap Compute Idea
bullets.body: NVIDIA announced a revenue-sharing and credit-support model with AI cloud partners (e.g., Sharon AI deploying up to 40K GB300 GPUs; Firmus building 360 MW campus), creating a recurring usage-linked earnings stream. Among mega-cap chips, NVDA moved ahead of AVGO as top idea due to strong HBM access vs. AVGO's 85% fulfillment rate. JPM models AI servers at +37% CAGR through 2030, with NVDA at ~50% AI DC switch share.

bullets.title: MU: UBS Raises PT to $1,625; June DRAM +52% QoQ; Supply Deficit Until 2Q28
bullets.body: UBS raised its 2H26 DDR contract pricing forecast to +32% QoQ in 3Q26 (vs. +17% prior) and +18% in 4Q26; NAND raised to +30% QoQ in 3Q26. DRAM industry forecast undersupplied until at least 2Q28 with 2027 bit demand growth (+36.2% YoY) far exceeding supply (+19.3%). Micron (Buy, $1,625 PT) signed Strategic Customer Agreements expanding from 1 to 16 contracts including GM; June DRAM monthly contract prices +52% QoQ, NAND +19.7% QoQ. Memory stocks pulled back 17% from June peak but UBS sees it as temporary.

bullets.title: TSM: 2027-28 Capex Raised to $75-80B; Analyst Lifts Estimates 13-21%
bullets.body: Laura Chen raises TSM 2027 estimates +13% and 2028 +21% to NT$3,800 target as TSM lifts 2027/2028 capex to $75-80B (from $68B/$75B) while keeping 2026 at $55B. CoWoS capacity now forecast to reach 130K/180K wpm by end-2026/27, with ASE's capacity to more than double to ~50K wpm by 2027. UBS models cloud AI segment at ~50% CAGR for advanced packaging over five years.

bullets.title: GOOGL: MS Raises PT to $415 on 2028 Cloud Capacity; EU €4.1B Antitrust Fine Upheld
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raises GOOGL PT to $415 (from $375, OW) as 2028 capacity expansion to 9 GW (7 GW TPU, 2 GW NVDA GPU) drives Google Cloud to $214B/$308B in 2027/2028—106%/44% growth. Cloud EBIT projected at $132B in 2028 (~46% of company-wide EBIT); 2028 EPS modeled at $19. Separately, the European Court of Justice upheld Google's €4.13B ($4.70B) Android antitrust fine and a Swedish court ordered a $1.5B Klarna damages payment.

bullets.title: CMCSA: Upgraded to Buy After NBCU/Sky Spinoff; CHTR Surges on SpaceX Mobile Talks
bullets.body: Comcast announced a tax-free spinoff of NBCUniversal and Sky (~1 year to close), with Mike Cavanagh as NBCU CEO and Michael Angelakis to lead the cable RemainCo. Deutsche Bank and Rosenblatt both upgraded CMCSA to Buy ($32/$31 PTs). Separately, CHTR held exec-level talks with SpaceX on a consumer mobile phone offering leveraging Spectrum's WiFi/small cell network. Wolfe Research upgraded FOXA to Outperform ($71 PT, 36% upside) as the $22B Roku deal doubles Fox's long-term growth trajectory.

bullets.title: AAPL: Cuts iPhone 17 Production ~15%; Seeks Chinese Memory Sourcing Approval
bullets.body: Apple reduced iPhone 17 production plans amid lower shipment forecasts and is in talks to source DRAM/NAND from Chinese suppliers CXMT and YMTC (both Pentagon-blacklisted), seeking White House political cover. Apple raised MacBook/iPad/Mac prices 15-25% citing unprecedented memory cost surges; iPhone 18 price hikes expected in September. UBS projects margins drop to 35.9% in the September quarter without pricing adjustments. Apple also faces ongoing EU Siri AI regulatory dispute.

bullets.title: FOXA Upgraded to Outperform at Wolfe; ROKU Deal Reshapes Narrative
bullets.body: Wolfe upgrades FOXA to Outperform with a $71 PT (36% upside, $80 SOTP fair value) after a 23% post-deal selloff. The $22B Roku acquisition doubles Fox's long-term sales CAGR and shifts the narrative from linear TV to multi-channel CTV compounder; streaming represents ~45% of engagement post-deal. Pro forma FOXA trades at 11.8x NTM UFCF with $400M cost synergies and untapped revenue upside. World Cup drove FS1 viewership +127% YoY.

bullets.title: HOOD: Raises PT at Mizuho ($130) and Piper ($135) on Global Brokerage Expansion
bullets.body: Mizuho raises HOOD PT to $130 (from $115) and Piper reiterates OW/$135 PT as Robinhood launched perpetual futures in Europe on gold, silver, oil, ETFs/currencies via Bitstamp with up to 10x leverage, tokenized stocks, a 7% APY stablecoin lending product, and its own blockchain. HOOD also added to Mizuho's July Top Picks list. June equity volumes tracked at record highs; the firm is expanding to Canada, UK crypto trading, and Singapore.

bullets.title: ADBE Upgraded to Buy at HSBC; AI Disruption Risk Seen as Overblown
bullets.body: HSBC upgrades ADBE from Hold to Buy, raising PT to $308 from $282 (46% upside), arguing AI disruption fears are overdone with no evidence of market share loss. PLTR also upgraded to Buy by DA Davidson ($175 PT, from $165) on growing 2x faster than peers at a discounted valuation (50x vs. prior 200x). PLTR's FCF margins doubled last year and are expected to double again.

bullets.title: DLR: Acquires Blackstone NOVA Data Centers for $7.8B; Citi Reiterates Buy
bullets.body: Digital Realty announced the acquisition of Blackstone's interest in three fully-leased Northern Virginia hyperscale data centers (288 MW) for $7.8B gross ($3.5B cash + $2.3B stock) at a >6.5% stabilized cap rate with 3.6% annual escalators. The deal is expected to add ~80bps to Core FFOPS in 2027 and ~330bps in 2028. Citi maintains Buy with a $226 PT (~18.6% upside). DLR raised ~$1.2B via ATM to partially fund the transaction.

bullets.title: VZ: JV with BT Group Triggers $700-800M Q2 Loss; Stock Hits 52-Week Low
bullets.body: Verizon announced a 50:50 joint venture with BT Group combining international operations (3,000+ customers, $4B combined revenue) and will pay BT a $625M equalization payment. VZ expects Q2 charges of up to $1.55B, including an $800M loss on reclassification of the contributed business. VZ hit a 52-week low amid broader telecom sector weakness on Starlink mobile competition fears.

bullets.title: SMCI: Taiwan Offices Raided in Chip-Smuggling Probe; Shares -8%
bullets.body: Taiwan authorities raided Super Micro Computer's offices as part of an expanded investigation into alleged NVIDIA chip smuggling into China. SMCI shares fell ~8% on the news. DELL and HPE shares moved higher in sympathy. The investigation adds brand and regulatory risk to SMCI, which is also raising up to $7B to fund ~$39B in AI server orders.

bullets.title: NOW and CRM: Guggenheim Upgrades Both to Buy; AI Bear Case 'Overdone'
bullets.body: Guggenheim upgraded CRM to Buy ($228 PT, 46% upside) and NOW to Buy ($125 PT, 26% upside), arguing AI will have a material but manageable impact on software, that current valuations imply perpetual decline, and that subscription revenue growth should stabilize and potentially accelerate in late 2026. CRM Agentforce ARR hit $1.2B in Q1 FY27, up 205% YoY.

bullets.title: DDOG: Acquires Adaptive ML for RLOps; Full AI Loop Closed
bullets.body: Datadog acquired Adaptive ML, a reinforcement learning operations startup founded by former Hugging Face engineers, for undisclosed terms. The deal gives DDOG a full AI loop: measure (LLM Observability), compare (Eppo), improve (Adaptive). DDOG can now run AI products on cheap in-house models, potentially improving gross margins by avoiding external API costs. Wolfe Research maintains DDOG as a long/alpha pick with 30%+ Atlas-style growth potential.

bullets.title: BE: Expands Brookfield AI Infrastructure Partnership 5x to $25B; MS Upgrades to OW
bullets.body: Bloom Energy expanded its AI infrastructure partnership with Brookfield to $25B (from $5B), implying 5 GW of fuel cell development potential vs. original 1 GW. Brookfield has already committed $1.6B across 6-7 projects (330 MW). Morgan Stanley upgraded BE to Overweight with a $310 PT, forecasting 14.6 GW aggregate deployments through decade-end.

bullets.title: TSLA: Q2 Deliveries Beat at 480K+, +25% YoY; Energy Storage Solid
bullets.body: Tesla reported Q2 deliveries of ~480K vehicles (+25% YoY, +34% QoQ), beating consensus of ~397-406K—the highest growth rate since Q3 2023 per Morgan Stanley. Energy storage came in at 13.5 GWh (+34% YoY), slightly below MS estimates but in line with consensus. EU registrations more than doubled in France and jumped 39-56% in Denmark/Sweden. Separately, Tesla is implementing weekly AI spend caps of $200 per employee starting July 6.

bullets.title: AFRM: Citi and Piper Both Initiate/Raise to Bullish; FY29 EPS Upside $5.00
bullets.body: Citi raised AFRM PT to $115 (from $100, Buy) citing >29% FY27 GMV growth and FY29 GAAP EPS potential of $5.00 vs consensus $3.72 (+34% upside). Piper Sandler also initiated AFRM at Overweight. 70%+ of top e-commerce merchants remain unintegrated, offering significant TAM runway. New merchant wins (Intuit, ServiceTitan, Lowe's, Costco) and Affirm Card support the bull case.

bullets.title: GS Prime: HFs Net Sold Tech for 4th Straight Week; Info Tech at -2.7 SDs
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs Prime Services reported hedge funds net sold US equities for a third straight week, with Info Tech the most net-sold sector for a fourth consecutive week (-2.7 SDs one-year). Semis & Semi Equipment and Tech Hardware led selling within Info Tech. Macro Products were net bought for a second straight week. Fundamental L/S performance fell -1.53% (6/26-7/2) vs. MSCI World +1.67%.
